description: What this shows: Peer connection quality: latency, divergence, version distribution and upgrade guidance, resource disconnects, and inbound/outbound balance.  —  Use it to: Assess how good this node's peer set is and whether connectivity or an upgrade needs attention.

panels.title: P90 Peer Latency
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*90th-percentile round-trip latency to connected peers, in milliseconds.*

###### How it's computed:
*Instantaneous gauge reading of the p90 peer latency.*

###### Reading it:
*Lower is better; green under 200ms, yellow to 500ms, red above.*

###### Healthy range:
*Under 200ms.*

###### Watch for:
*Rising latency, which points to network congestion or geographically distant, poorly performing peers.*

###### Keywords:
- **Peer** *(per node)* — another server this node holds a protocol connection to.
- **Overlay** *(network-wide)* — the peer-to-peer mesh xrpld nodes form to gossip transactions, proposals and validations.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Computed in xrpld code (AppMetricGauges, OpenTelemetry SDK) and exported as a metric; the collector only forwards it; the Grafana query selects and aggregates it.*

###### Source:
[AppMetricGauges.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/AppMetricGauges.cpp)

###### Function:
`registerPeerQualityGauge`

###### References:
[Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#ping-pong-keepalive)

panels.title: Insane/Diverged Peers [$xrpl_network_type]
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Count of connected peers whose ledger state has diverged from the network.*

###### How it's computed:
*Instantaneous gauge reading of the diverged-peer count.*

###### Reading it:
*Zero is healthy; any count means those peers disagree on ledger state.*

###### Healthy range:
*0 diverged peers.*

###### Watch for:
*A persistent non-zero count, which can indicate peers on a fork or misbehaving peers.*

###### Keywords:
- **Insane / diverged peers** *(per node)* — connected peers whose ledger state disagrees with the network — possibly on a fork or misbehaving.
- **Fork** *(network-wide)* — when nodes validate divergent ledger chains instead of a single agreed history.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Computed in xrpld code (AppMetricGauges, OpenTelemetry SDK) and exported as a metric; the collector only forwards it; the Grafana query selects and aggregates it.*

###### Source:
[AppMetricGauges.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/AppMetricGauges.cpp)

###### Function:
`registerPeerQualityGauge`

###### References:
[Fork](https://xrpl.org/docs/concepts/consensus-protocol) · [Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#insane-diverged-peers)

panels.title: Higher Version Peers % [$xrpl_network_type]
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Percentage of connected peers running a newer rippled version than this node.*

###### How it's computed:
*Instantaneous gauge reading of the higher-version peer percentage.*

###### Reading it:
*A high percentage suggests this node is behind and should be upgraded.*

###### Healthy range:
*Under 30%.*

###### Watch for:
*A majority of peers on a newer version, a strong upgrade signal.*

###### Keywords:
- **Peer** *(per node)* — another server this node holds a protocol connection to.
- **Overlay** *(network-wide)* — the peer-to-peer mesh xrpld nodes form to gossip transactions, proposals and validations.

###### Computation boundary:

panels.title: Upgrade Recommended [$xrpl_network_type]
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*A flag indicating whether an upgrade is advised based on peer version analysis (Yes/No).*

###### How it's computed:
*Instantaneous gauge reading of the upgrade-recommended flag.*

###### Reading it:
*No is healthy; Yes means most peers run a newer version.*

###### Healthy range:
*No.*

###### Watch for:
*A Yes state, indicating the node risks falling out of step with the network.*

###### Keywords:
- **Peer** *(per node)* — another server this node holds a protocol connection to.
- **Overlay** *(network-wide)* — the peer-to-peer mesh xrpld nodes form to gossip transactions, proposals and validations.

panels.title: Inbound vs Outbound Peers [$xrpl_network_type]
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Active inbound versus outbound peer connection counts.*

###### How it's computed:
*Instantaneous gauge readings of active inbound and outbound peer counts.*

###### Reading it:
*A balanced mix is healthy for connectivity and resilience.*

###### Healthy range:
*A mix of both; some outbound connections present.*

###### Watch for:
*All-inbound with no outbound, which usually means NAT or firewall issues block outbound peering.*

###### Keywords:
- **Peer** *(per node)* — another server this node holds a protocol connection to.
- **Overlay** *(network-wide)* — the peer-to-peer mesh xrpld nodes form to gossip transactions, proposals and validations.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Recorded in xrpld code as a native metric (beast::insight); the collector only forwards it; the Grafana query selects and aggregates it.*

###### Source:
[PeerfinderManager.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/libxrpl/peerfinder/PeerfinderManager.cpp)

###### Function:
`ManagerImp::collectMetrics (gauges made in ManagerImp::Stats)`

###### References:
[Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#overlay)

panels.title: Busiest Peer Share
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*The busiest peer's share of the validations this node receives, for trusted and for untrusted signers.*

###### How it's computed:
*The node counts the validations each peer delivers. At each collection it turns the counts into per-second rates and divides the busiest peer's rate by the total for that trust class. 0 when no validations arrived.*

###### Reading it:
*Near 1 means one peer carries almost all of that traffic. Traffic spread over many peers keeps it low.*

###### Healthy range:
*Well below 1 on a node with several peers.*

###### Watch for:
*An untrusted share near 1 during an untrusted validation flood: one peer carries it. Validation Load Warnings names that peer when it is over the per-peer limit.*

###### Keywords:
- **Peer** *(per node)* — another server this node holds a protocol connection to.
- **Trusted / untrusted** *(per node)* — a validation is trusted when its signer is on this node's UNL, untrusted otherwise.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Computed in xrpld code (AppMetricGauges, OpenTelemetry SDK) and exported as a metric; the collector only forwards it; the Grafana query selects it.*

###### Source:
[AppMetricGauges.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/AppMetricGauges.cpp)

###### Function:
`registerPeerValidationLoadGauge`

###### References:
[Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#validation-load)

panels.title: Top-3 Peer Validation Rates
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Validations per second from the three busiest peers, for trusted and for untrusted signers.*

###### How it's computed:
*The node counts the validations each peer delivers, including duplicates and untrusted ones it then drops. At each collection it turns the counts into per-second rates since the previous collection and reports the three highest for each trust class. A rank follows whichever peer was busiest in that interval, not one fixed peer.*

###### Reading it:
*Top 1 far above Top 2 and Top 3 means one peer sends most of the traffic. Lines close together mean the load is spread.*

###### Healthy range:
*Untrusted Top 1 under the per-peer warning limit, so Validation Load Warnings stays empty.*

###### Watch for:
*Untrusted Top 1 rising far above Top 2 during a flood: one peer carries it.*

###### Keywords:
- **Peer** *(per node)* — another server this node holds a protocol connection to.
- **Trusted / untrusted** *(per node)* — a validation is trusted when its signer is on this node's UNL, untrusted otherwise.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Computed in xrpld code (AppMetricGauges, OpenTelemetry SDK) and exported as a metric; the collector only forwards it; the Grafana query selects it.*

###### Source:
[AppMetricGauges.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/AppMetricGauges.cpp)

###### Function:
`registerPeerValidationLoadGauge`

###### References:
[Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#validation-load)

panels.title: Validation Load Warnings
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Warning lines that name the busiest peer when its untrusted validation rate is over the per-peer limit.*

###### How it's computed:
*Raw log stream filtered to WRN lines that contain "Validation load: peer". Each line gives the peer's connection id, its node public key and its untrusted validations per second. The throttle is per connection: one connection is named at most once every five minutes, and a reconnect gets a new id.*

###### Reading it:
*Look the public key up in the peers admin command, which shows the peer's address while it is connected.*

###### Healthy range:
*Empty.*

###### Watch for:
*The same public key every few minutes: that peer keeps flooding this node.*

###### Keywords:
- **Log stream** *(per node)* — the raw lines behind the aggregate rates, newest first.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Raw log lines, no aggregation.*
*Rendered directly from Loki; no computation applied.*

###### Source:
[AppMetricGauges.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/AppMetricGauges.cpp)

###### Function:
`registerPeerValidationLoadGauge`

###### References:
[Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#validation-load)

targets.expr: {service_name=~"$service_name", service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment"} |= `Validation load: peer` | xrpl_network_type =~ "$xrpl_network_type" | severity = `WRN` | line_format `{{.partition}}:{{.severity}} {{.message}}`

panels.title: Resource Disconnects
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How many peers per minute this node drops for exceeding resource (load) limits.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-minute rate of the resource-disconnect total over the rate interval. The total starts again from zero after a restart; the rate treats that as a restart, not a fall.*

###### Reading it:
*Zero is healthy; any line above zero means peers are being dropped for overuse.*

###### Healthy range:
*At or near zero.*

###### Watch for:
*A sustained non-zero rate, which flags aggressive or misbehaving peers being shed as backpressure.*

###### Keywords:
- **Resource disconnect** *(per node)* — a peer dropped for exceeding resource/load limits — the node shedding abusive or overactive peers.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Computed in xrpld code (AppMetricGauges, OpenTelemetry SDK) and exported as a metric; the collector only forwards it; the Grafana query selects and aggregates it.*

###### Source:
[AppMetricGauges.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/telemetry/AppMetricGauges.cpp)

###### Function:
`registerServerInfoGauge`

###### References:
[Telemetry glossary](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#resource-disconnect)

panels.title: Peer Disconnect Rate
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*How many peer connections per minute this node closes, across all reasons.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-minute rate of the peer-disconnect counter over the rate interval, summed per node. Narrow it with the Disconnect Reason and Disconnect Direction variables.*

###### Reading it:
*A low, steady rate is ordinary churn. The height of the line says how fast the peer set is turning over, not why — pair it with Peer Disconnects By Reason & Direction for the cause.*

###### Healthy range:
*Low and steady relative to each node's own baseline.*

###### Watch for:
*A sustained rise, which means the peer set is churning faster than it is being replaced and can leave the node short of peers to sync from. Distinct from Resource Disconnects, which counts only the resource-charge subset and carries no reason breakdown.*

###### Keywords:
- **Peer disconnect** *(per node)* — a peer connection closed by this node, for any reason, counted once per teardown.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Computed in xrpld code (call-site metric macro, OpenTelemetry SDK) and exported as a metric; the collector only forwards it; the Grafana query selects and aggregates it.*

###### Source:
[PeerImp.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/overlay/detail/PeerImp.cpp)

###### Function:
`PeerImp::close`

###### References:
[Disconnect reason](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#disconnect-reason)

targets.expr: label_replace(label_join(label_replace(sum by (service_instance_id, xrpl_branch, xrpl_work_item) (rate(peer_disconnect_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", xrpl_work_item=~"$xrpl_work_item", xrpl_branch=~"$xrpl_branch", xrpl_node_role=~"$xrpl_node_role", reason=~"$disconnect_reason", direction=~"$disconnect_direction"}[$__rate_interval])) * 60, "series", "Peer Disconnects / Min", "", ""), "xrpl_ident", ", ", "service_instance_id", "xrpl_branch", "xrpl_work_item"), "xrpl_ident", "[$1]", "xrpl_ident", "(?:, )*(.*[^, ])(?:, )*")

panels.title: Peer Disconnects By Reason & Direction
panels.description:
###### What this is:
*Peer closes per minute, split by why they closed and by which side opened the connection.*

###### How it's computed:
*Per-minute rate of the peer-disconnect counter over the rate interval, grouped by node, reason and direction. It is a rate, not a count per point. Each point's window overlaps the next, so a count would show one disconnect more than once. Filter with the Disconnect Reason and Disconnect Direction variables.*

###### Reading it:
*The split tells slow or overactive peers apart from topology and network faults. large_sendq is this node dropping a peer whose send queue stayed full for several minutes: the peer, or the path to it, did not take data as fast as this node sent it. charge_resources is this node cutting off a peer whose traffic used up its resource allowance: too many messages, costly requests, or bad data. not_useful and ping_timeout are topology and liveness. read_error is a failed read. It includes a peer simply closing the connection: xrpld drops a peer without starting a TLS shutdown, so between xrpld nodes an ordinary close lands here, not under graceful. A network fault, or a malformed or oversized message, lands here too. write_error is a failed write. graceful, stopping and shutdown are ordinary lifecycle, not faults.*

###### Healthy range:
*A low, steady read_error rate (ordinary churn) and the other reasons near zero. graceful stays near zero between xrpld nodes.*

###### Watch for:
*A sustained large_sendq on many peers at once points at this node's own uplink; on a few peers, at those peers or the path to them. A sustained charge_resources points at peers that send too much or send bad data, not at this node. A rising not_useful or ping_timeout on outbound points at the peer set instead. This is the time-shaped view of the split; the Ledger Sync Health dashboard carries the same split as a window total.*

###### Keywords:
- **Peer disconnect reason** *(per node)* — the cause recorded when a peer connection is closed, paired with whether that connection was inbound or outbound.

###### Computation boundary:
*Result: Per node — each series is one server's own value.*
*Computed in xrpld code (call-site metric macro, OpenTelemetry SDK) and exported as a metric; the collector only forwards it; the Grafana query selects and aggregates it.*

###### Source:
[PeerImp.cpp](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/src/xrpld/overlay/detail/PeerImp.cpp)

###### Function:
`PeerImp::close`

###### References:
[Disconnect reason](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#disconnect-reason) · [Insane / diverged peers](https://github.com/XRPLF/rippled/blob/develop/docs/telemetry-glossary.md#insane-diverged-peers)

targets.expr: label_replace(label_join(label_join(sum by (reason, direction, service_instance_id, xrpl_branch, xrpl_work_item) (rate(peer_disconnect_total{service_instance_id=~"$node", deployment_environment=~"$deployment_environment", xrpl_network_type=~"$xrpl_network_type", service_name=~"$service_name", xrpl_work_item=~"$xrpl_work_item", xrpl_branch=~"$xrpl_branch", xrpl_node_role=~"$xrpl_node_role", reason=~"$disconnect_reason", direction=~"$disconnect_direction"}[$__rate_interval])) * 60, "series", " ", "reason", "direction"), "xrpl_ident", ", ", "service_instance_id", "xrpl_branch", "xrpl_work_item"), "xrpl_ident", "[$1]", "xrpl_ident", "(?:, )*(.*[^, ])(?:, )*")
